name: Hanty
catalog_quote: In words of all sizes, primary stress falls on the initial syllable. In words of all sizes, secondary stress falls iteratively on odd numbered syllables, counting from the left.
sweep_summary: Three titles searched for khan1273 (catalog: fixed-strict, initial primary + odd-syllable secondaries, from a StressTyp2 template resting on Rédei 1965, unobtained). All three were read in full: Belkind 2023 (Glossa, open, downloaded past the site's bot wall) is Kazym phrase-prosody and says only in fn. 14 that word stress is cued by intensity and length, deferring to Kaksin 2010 — silent on placement. Fil'chenko 2011 (Vestnik TGPU, open via Cyberleninka) is Eastern Khanty sentence intonation, a different language, silent on stress placement. Normanskaja 2014 (already held by the project) is Nizyam/Irtysh data with mobile stress, but states that most north-western dialects and specifically Kazym have stress always on the first syllable (pp. 285-286), while Shuryshkar (Suryskarer, a child dialect of khan1273) is 'clearly mobile' — a refinement that partly contradicts fixed-strict. Best first-hand statement: Kaksin 2010 sec. 2.4 pp. 34-37 (held by the project, cited by Belkind): default initial stress, secondary on syllable 3, but stress shifts to a long-vowel second syllable (trisyllables with short first vowel; any 4+-syllable word). This supersedes the catalog's template-only source; the odd-syllable iteration beyond syllable 3 is not attested in any source read. g. Rédei 1965) were hunted.

new_statements.quote: «С точки зрения структурной типологии ударение в казымском диалекте в целом связанное фиксированное: оно падает обычно на первый слог (но есть некоторые отклонения от этого правила, которые связаны со слоговой структурой слова).» (p. 34) «В словах с четырьмя и более слогами ударение падает на второй слог, если гласный этого слога является долгим.» (p. 36) «В многосложном слове появляется два ударения. Главное ударение падает на первый слог, а добавочное ударение – на третий слог.» (pp. 36-37)
new_statements.translation: 'From the standpoint of structural typology, stress in the Kazym dialect is on the whole bound and fixed: it usually falls on the first syllable (but there are some deviations from this rule, connected with the syllable structure of the word).' 'In words of four or more syllables stress falls on the second syllable if the vowel of that syllable is long.' 'In a polysyllabic word two stresses appear. The main stress falls on the first syllable and the secondary stress on the third syllable.'
new_statements.citation: Kaksin, A. D. 2010. Kazymskij dialekt khantyjskogo jazyka. 2nd ed. Khanty-Mansijsk: IIC JuGU. Section 2.4 'Udarenie', pp. 34-37 (open copy https://ouipiir.ru/sites/default/files/docs/85-1201.pdf; cited by Belkind 2023 fn. 14 as the source for Kazym stress).
new_statements.reading: Kazym Khanty (the dialect underlying the literary standard and the core of khan1273) has initial primary stress as the default, with a secondary stress on the third syllable in longer words (p. 36-37; examples marked wa.sεŋә:łәm 'my two ducks', mu.χsәŋә:tәn 'with muksun fish'). But stress is not strictly fixed: in trisyllables it moves to a second syllable containing long [a] or [ε] when the first vowel is short (p. 36, e.g. păsana 'onto the table', mănεma 'to me'), and in words of four or more syllables it falls on the second syllable whenever that vowel is long, regardless of the first vowel (p. 36, e.g. păsa.nәta, kełε.mәna). Kaksin says nothing about stresses beyond the third syllable, so the catalog's iterative 'every odd syllable' template is not attested in the source. The catalog's initial primary + secondary on syllable 3 is confirmed as the default; the 'fixed-strict' label is refined by the vowel-length-driven second-syllable stress (a quantity-sensitive exception), and Normanskaja 2014 adds that the Shuryshkar dialect within this languoid has mobile stress.

audit.recode_to: From 'fixed-strict' (initial, counts as exceptionless (the strict set)) to a non-strict / quantity-sensitive initial-default class: primary stress on σ1 by default, but on σ2 when σ2 has a long (full) vowel [a]/[ε] and σ1 is short (trisyllables), and on σ2 whenever its vowel is long in words of 4+ syllables (Kaksin 2010:36); secondary stress on σ3 (σ5..) retained (Kaksin 2010:37; Rédei 1965:28 via Kashkin 2020:35). I.e. a left-edge two-syllable window with vowel-length sensitivity, not strict fixed initial; cite Kaksin 2010 sec. 2.4 pp. 34-37 as deciding source, with Nemysova et al. 2023:8 as supporting 'основное ударение.. на первый слог'.

sources.quote: p. 23: "All prosodic units smaller than intonational phrase are left-headed (42), i.e. for each prosodic phrase, the most prominent, high-pitched element is located at the left boundary". Footnote 14 (p. 23): "Khanty has a canonical stress system, where word stress is realized with intensity and length (Kaksin 2010, V. Tyutyunnikova p.c. for Kazym Khanty, Normanskaja 2014 for Nizjam Khanty). Pitch hight only marks heads of prosodic and intonational phrases."
sources.note: First-hand Kazym Khanty fieldwork on phrase-level prominence (phonological/intonational phrasing, pitch accents H*+L, clitic ki attaches to the most prominent phonological phrase). Word stress is mentioned only in footnote 14: it exists, is cued by intensity and length, and pitch marks phrase heads rather than word stress. No statement of where word stress falls; defers to Kaksin 2010. Silent on the catalog's initial-plus-odd-syllable coding.
